questions.stem: What is produced when ethanol is oxidised?
questions.explanation: When ethanol is oxidised (e.g., by chemical oxidising agents or by microbial action), it forms ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH), a carboxylic acid. This is why wine turns to vinegar.

questions.stem: What happens when ethanol reacts with sodium metal?

options.text: Sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas are produced
Sodium chloride and water are produced

questions.explanation: Ethanol reacts gently with sodium to produce sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂. This is less vigorous than sodium reacting with water.

questions.stem: What type of reaction occurs when ethanol is dehydrated?
questions.explanation: Dehydration of ethanol is an elimination reaction where water is removed from the alcohol to form ethene: C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O. This requires a strong acid catalyst or hot aluminium oxide.

questions.stem: What is formed when ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid in the presence of an acid catalyst?
questions.explanation: An alcohol + a carboxylic acid → an ester + water. This is called an esterification reaction and requires an acid catalyst (usually concentrated sulfuric acid).

questions.stem: Ethanol burns with a clean blue flame. Why is ethanol used as a fuel?

options.text: It is the only liquid fuel
It is the cheapest fuel available
It burns cleanly, releases energy, and can be made from renewable plant sources
It does not produce any emissions when burned

questions.explanation: Ethanol is useful as a fuel because it burns cleanly (producing CO₂ and H₂O), releases a good amount of energy, and can be produced renewably from the fermentation of plant material.

questions.stem: Which reagent is commonly used to oxidise ethanol to ethanoic acid in the laboratory?
questions.explanation: Acidified potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) is used to oxidise alcohols. It changes colour from orange to green during the reaction, confirming oxidation has occurred.

questions.stem: Which catalyst is used for the dehydration of ethanol to produce ethene?

options.text: Hot aluminium oxide or concentrated sulfuric acid

questions.explanation: Hot aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃) or concentrated sulfuric acid can be used as catalysts to dehydrate ethanol, removing water and producing ethene.
